reader_question: Which sectors added jobs since January 2022, and which lost them?
grade_line: Documented: a Bureau of Labor Statistics survey of employers, as copied by FRED
title: Health care and social assistance added 3.8 million jobs from January 2022 to September 2026, the most of any industry; information and the federal government lost jobs.
measure_line: Payroll jobs by industry, seasonally adjusted, change since January 2022 in percent, United States, January 2022 to September 2026, the span both jobs charts share.
notes: The first rows hold the totals: all nonfarm jobs, its two parts, private industries and government, and federal jobs, which are part of government. The 14 panels below add up to private industries.
Seasonally adjusted: the Bureau removes the swings that recur each year, such as summer hiring and holiday layoffs, so one month compares with the next.

The Bureau publishes no sampling error for a change over this many months. For employment levels it gives standard errors of 0.1 to 0.9 percent in these industries, smaller than a 90 percent margin of error, and none for government (Bureau of Labor Statistics, All Employees Standard Error Tables. Retrieved November 11, 2026).
Government, all levels, gained 1.3 million jobs and federal jobs fell by 197,000, so state and local payrolls, which this dataset does not carry on their own, grew by about 1.5 million.
Federal government jobs peaked at 3,013,000 in October 2024 and stood at 2,682,000 in September 2026.
August and September 2026 are preliminary: the Bureau of Labor Statistics revises each month’s first estimate in the next two monthly reports, and a yearly benchmark revision can move earlier months.
Both jobs charts run from January 2022 to September 2026, so they hold three full years before the January 2025 inauguration and every month since.
source_line: Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics, all employees by industry, seasonally adjusted, January 2022 to September 2026, United States, via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Retrieved November 6, 2026. August and September 2026 are preliminary and will be revised.
alt: A sparkline table of the payroll total, its two parts and federal jobs, above 14 small area charts of the private industries, January 2022 to September 2026, on one scale of percent change. All nonfarm jobs rose 9.0 million, 6.0 percent. Health care and social assistance gained the most, 3.8 million jobs or 18.8 percent; information lost 245,000 jobs, 8.2 percent, and the federal government lost 197,000, 6.8 percent.

table.caption: Change in payroll jobs since January 2022, percent, by month and series

chart_notes: The total, its two parts and federal jobs, each with its change since January 2022: all nonfarm jobs +9.0 million, +6.0%; private industries +7.8 million, +6.1%; government, all levels, +1.3 million, +5.8%; federal government −197,000, −6.8%. Federal jobs peaked at 3,013,000 in October 2024.

Private industries, largest percent gain first. Gray line in every panel: all nonfarm jobs, +6.0%. Each panel ends with the change in jobs and in percent since January 2022, and its scale runs from −15 to +20 percent, January 2022 to September 2026.
